The “normal” keyword being described as “Default value” in Values is not the same as reading the Formal definition “Initial value” row, and “Applies to: all elements” is entirely unsupported by the visible page area. This violates the task constraint to report unavailable fields as unavailable rather than guessing.

What is actually supported: The Syntax code block visible in Screenshot 1 clearly lists keyword values normal, size, inline-size, scroll-state, anchored (and shows “size scroll-state” as a two-value example). So the keyword list portion is correct.

Overall outcome: The task required five deliverables (initial value, applies to, formal-syntax keywords, and three desktop compatibility entries). The agent only provides one of these with evidentiary support (the keywords). The other required items are effectively unverified/likely guessed, which would not satisfy the user’s primary intent of accurately recording MDN’s formal definition and compatibility data.

The “normal” keyword being described as “Default value” in Values is not the same as reading the Formal definition “Initial value” row, and “Applies to: all elements” is entirely unsupported by the visible page area. (2) The agent reports specific desktop browser compatibility minimum versions (Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) without ever displaying the Browser compatibility section/table in screenshots, and the action history shows only a single scroll action; there is no evidence those version numbers were actually taken from MDN’s base-property desktop compatibility entries. This violates the task constraint to report unavailable fields as unavailable rather than guessing.

What is actually supported: The Syntax code block visible in Screenshot 1 clearly lists keyword values normal, size, inline-size, scroll-state, anchored (and shows “size scroll-state” as a two-value example). So the keyword list portion is correct.

Overall outcome: The task required five deliverables (initial value, applies to, formal-syntax keywords, and three desktop compatibility entries). The agent only provides one of these with evidentiary support (the keywords). The other required items are effectively unverified/likely guessed, which would not satisfy the user’s primary intent of accurately recording MDN’s formal definition and compatibility data.
